Data Status Check

Elham Ebrahimi

Source: vignettes/articles/data-status-report.Rmd
data-status-report.Rmd

Purpose of the Data Status Check

The Data Status Check summarises the quality, completeness, and internal consistency of a camera-trap dataset before ecological reporting. It checks the main input files, metadata, deployments, observations, taxonomy, timestamps, annotations, and spatial information.

The output helps users identify missing values, duplicated records, invalid timestamps, incomplete metadata, spatial issues, and inconsistencies between deployments and observations. It is diagnostic: completing the checks does not establish that the survey design or data are suitable for a particular ecological analysis.

Figure 1 summarises the automated workflow. camData() reads the camera-trap dataset and prepares it for reporting. status() then runs the implemented checks and generates the HTML Data Status Check.

Figure 1. Workflow for generating a Data Status Check from camera-trap data using camtrapReport. 

library(camtrapReport)

cm <- camData("path/to/camtrap-dp-dataset")
status(cm, view = TRUE)

These two function calls are sufficient for the standard workflow. With view = TRUE, the generated report opens in the browser. status() also invisibly returns the path to the HTML file.

To retain the report at a chosen location, supply a filename in an existing output directory:

status_file <- status(cm, filename = "reports/data_status_2026", view = FALSE)

If filename is omitted, the HTML file and its intermediate R Markdown file are written to the R session’s temporary directory. Use distinct filenames when reports from several datasets or processing dates must be retained.

Accessing results in R

The results are also stored in the camReport object and can be accessed when individual tables or summaries are needed for further analysis.

# List the available result components
names(cm$data_status)

# Inspect the species summary table
cm$data_status$Species$Table

For most users, the generated HTML report is the main output. Direct access through cm$data_status is optional.
